front: Wide brown tail, white underneath, held up and waving. Which deer?
back: White tailed deer. The raised tail is the flag (85%).

front: Thin white rope tail with a black tip on a big white rump. Which deer?
back: Mule deer (85%).

front: How do white tail antlers grow?
back: One main beam sweeping forward, tines rising straight up off it (85%).

front: What is the brow tine?
back: G1: the short tine just above the antler base (70%).

front: How does a white tail run from danger?
back: Low, smooth gallop with the tail up. A mule deer stots on all 4 feet (85%).

front: Best first clue to a buck's age on the hoof?
back: Body shape: neck, chest, belly, leg look. Not antlers (65%).

front: What does a yearling buck look like?
back: A doe with antlers: lanky, thin neck, narrow waist, long legs (65%).

front: Signs of a buck 4 years or older?
back: Deep chest, sagging belly, thick neck blending into shoulders, legs look short (65%).

front: Is a button buck legal in a bucks only season?
back: No. A button buck has no visible antlers, so it is antlerless (99%, synopsis page 3).

front: How common are mule deer and white tail hybrids on the western Canadian prairies?
back: About 1% (85%, Russell and others 2021). Not sure what it is? Do not shoot.

front: Average live weight of a white tail buck and doe (Idaho)?
back: Buck about 91 kg (200 lb), doe about 57 kg (125 lb) (80%).

front: Mature white tail buck weight (Montana)?
back: 91 to 136 kg (200 to 300 lb). Does 25 to 40% less (80%).

front: Which BC region had the most resident white tail kills in 2024?
back: Region 4 Kootenay, about 3,971 (90%).

front: Region 3 Thompson resident white tail kills, 2024?
back: About 1,091 from about 7,900 hunters, about 14% (90%).

front: MU 3-27 white tails taken per year, 2020 to 2024?
back: About 97 to 145 a year; 133 in 2024, about 17% success (90%).

front: Is there a white tail season in Region 2 (Fraser Valley)?
back: No. The Region 2 white tailed deer bag is 0 (97%, page 14).

front: BC white tail numbers, 1987 and 2011?
BC white tail estimate for 2022?
back: 35,000 to 71,500 (75%). Different method from 2011: compare with care.

front: Subspecies of southern Interior white tails?
back: Northwest white tail, Odocoileus virginianus ochrourus (75%).

front: Where are the lungs?
back: Filling the chest from just behind the shoulder back to the diaphragm (85%).

front: Where is the heart?
back: Low in the chest, near the elbows (80%).

front: What muscle drives breathing?
back: The diaphragm, between chest and belly (90%).

front: Why does a double lung hit kill fast?
back: Air enters the chest and the lungs collapse; the deer runs on stored oxygen, often 50 to 137 m (70%).

front: What covers the front of the lungs?
back: The shoulder blade, which slides with the leg (80%).

front: Where to aim on a broadside white tail?
back: Up the back of the front leg, one third up the chest (75%).

front: How many stomach chambers?
back: 4: rumen, reticulum, omasum, abomasum (85%).

front: What does the rumen do?
back: Holds microbes that ferment plant food (85%).

front: Why can a white tail starve on hay in a hard winter?
back: Rumen microbes need time to adjust to a new diet (80%, Montana State University Extension).

front: How much dry food does a white tail eat a day?
back: 2 to 4% of its body weight (80%).

front: When is a buck fattest?
back: About September, before the rut. He burns it in November (75%).

front: When are white tails leanest?
back: Late winter (80%).

front: How long do white tails live?
back: Few past 10 years; possible 20 plus (85%).

front: Average life of a buck in heavily hunted Pennsylvania?
back: About 2 years; does about 3 (85%, US Forest Service review).

front: Snow depth that makes deer travel hard?
back: Over about 40 cm (16 in) (85%).

front: What is yarding?
back: In hard winters deer bunch in dense cover and pack trails (80%).

front: A white tail's strongest sense?
back: Smell (85%).

front: Which way does your scent go on a sunny morning?
back: Uphill: warming air rises (80%).

front: Which way does your scent go in the evening?
back: Downhill, pooling in the river bottoms where white tails bed (80%).

front: Deer hearing range and best band?
back: About 115 Hz to 54 kHz, best 4 to 8 kHz (85%).

front: Which sounds hit a deer's best hearing band?
back: Zippers, Velcro, nylon, metal clicks, snapping twigs (85%).

front: White tail field of view?
back: About 310 degrees without turning the head (80%).

front: Where is a white tail's blind spot?
back: A narrow wedge straight behind (80%).

front: Why does blaze orange look dull to deer?
back: 2 colour cones (blue, green), no red cone (85%).

front: What gives a hunter away to a deer's eyes?
back: Motion and outline, not colour (85%).

front: What does an unsure white tail often do?
back: Circles downwind to smell you (Tip, widely reported).

front: Why sit high or in a dark blind?
back: Gets you out of the eye level scan of a horizontal pupil (Tip).

front: Legal status of deer urine lures from outside BC?
back: Unlawful for hunting (95%, page 12 item 51).

front: A doe stamps and stares. What do you do?
back: Freeze. The stamp is a test to make you move (Tip).

front: How many white tail calls did Atkeson and others record?
Which call marks a dominant buck's challenge in the rut?
back: Grunt snort wheeze (80%).

front: What is a tending grunt?
back: A long drawn out grunt a buck makes with a doe (70%).

front: Why does a white tail flag?
back: Debated: warn others, tell the predator it is seen, or guide fawns. One study found little support for warning others (70%).

front: Where does a spooked white tail run?
back: To the nearest thick cover, often stopping just inside to look back (Tip).

front: Penn State collar study: what did deer do on opening day?
back: Reacted the day before, then hid inside their home range (70%).

front: Who lives in a white tail family group?
back: An old doe, her daughters and their fawns (80%).

front: Size of a summer bachelor group?
back: 2 to 4 bucks (80%).

front: What share of yearling bucks disperse?
back: About 70%, mostly October and November (80%).

front: Do mature buck home ranges grow with age?
back: Collar study reviews say they often shrink (65%).

front: How many bedding areas did the average Mississippi collared buck use?
back: About 31 in a season; repeat beds had dense screening cover (65%).

front: White tail vs mule deer bucks: which fight more?
back: White tails (75%, Montana State University Extension). That is why rattling works.

front: When are white tail fawns born?
back: Late May or June (85%).

front: Gestation length?
back: About 202 days, about 7 months (80%).

front: How long is a newborn fawn hidden?
back: About 2 weeks; the doe returns to nurse 4 to 6 times a day (75 to 80%).

front: When do bucks rub off velvet?
back: Early to mid September (75%).

front: When do bucks drop antlers?
back: About January to March (75%).

front: What drives the antler cycle?
back: Day length acting through testosterone (75%).

front: When do most does conceive?
back: About 13 to 17 November (80%, Penn State). BC: rut peaks in November (85%).

front: How long is a doe in heat?
back: About 24 hours (80%).

front: Doe not bred? When is her next heat?
back: About 28 days later: the December second rut (80%).

front: How long does a buck tend a doe?
back: 1 to 3 days before her heat, 2 or 3 after (80%).

front: Rut phases in order?
back: Pre rut, seeking, chasing, tending (lockdown), post rut, second rut (60%).

front: Region 3 white tail buck season (2026 to 2028)?
back: 10 September to 10 December in the listed MUs (99%, page 34).

front: Antlerless white tails in Regions 3 and 8?
back: 10 to 31 October, no draw (99%, pages 34 and 68).

front: When do white tails move most?
back: Near dawn and dusk (85%).

front: When are white tails active most of the day?
back: Winter (85%, BC account).

front: Which factor predicts movement best: moon, barometer or time of day?
back: Time of day, then season (75%).

front: Do deer feed hard before a storm?
back: Penn State: no change before 30 winter storms; less movement during (80%).

front: Does the moon move white tails?
back: Collar studies: small or no effect; dawn and dusk win (75%).

front: How much water does a deer drink on dry food?
back: About 3 kg per kg of dry food (80%).

front: When should you be in your evening stand?
back: About 2 hours before dark (Tip).

front: Legal hunting hours?
back: 1 hour before sunrise to 1 hour after sunset (99%, page 11 item 38).

front: Classic white tail habitat?
back: Valley bottoms with farmland, river brush and edges (85%).

front: Where do valley white tails bed?
back: Willow, cottonwood, young conifers near water (75%).

front: White tail winter browse favourites?
back: Willow, red osier dogwood, chokecherry, saskatoon (80%).

front: White tail elevation in southern BC?
back: About 300 to 900 m most months (60 to 70%).

front: How far do white tails move to winter range?
back: Usually under 16 km (85%).

front: Which Hunt Map layer shows white tails by month?
back: White tailed deer by month (general pattern).

front: Which Hunt Map tool finds south facing slopes?
back: Slope direction (Tip: late season feed).

front: Top Region 3 MUs for white tails, 2022 to 2024?
Region 8 white tail bag limit?
back: 2: no more than 1 buck and 1 antlerless (99%, page 67).

front: White tail track: shape and size?
back: Heart shaped, 2 toes, about 4 to 10 cm, point shows direction (70 to 85%).

front: Gallop track pattern?
back: Groups of 4, hind prints ahead of front prints (75%).

front: Pellet size?
back: About 1 to 1.5 cm (70%).

front: A deer bed: what to look for?
back: Pressed oval about 1 m, hair, melted frost, pellets beside it (75%).

front: Which gland marks rubs?
back: Forehead gland between the antler bases (65%).

front: What is a scrape?
back: Pawed bare dirt under a licking branch, often with urine (75%).

front: Licking branch height?
back: About 1.2 to 1.5 m (4 to 5 ft) (65%, Ozoga).

front: Deer browse or hare browse?
back: Deer tear twigs (no upper front teeth). Hares cut clean at 45 degrees (75%).

front: Can a dog track your wounded deer?
back: Yes, on a leash only (99%, page 12).

front: Lost a blood trail. What now?
back: Small loops out from the last marked sign (Tip).

front: Beginner's best white tail method with farm permission?
back: A stand on the trail between bedding and food, downwind (Tip).

front: When does rattling work best?
back: Late October to mid November, cool calm mornings (70%).

front: Rattling response in the Texas study?
back: About 65% of bucks responded (70%).

front: Where does the shooter sit when rattling?
back: Downwind of the caller: bucks circle downwind (Tip).

front: Electronic deer calls in BC?
back: Not allowed for deer (99%).

front: Hunting with a partner: first rule?
back: Agree on zones of fire. Never shoot toward each other (Tip).

front: Wind wrong for plan A stand?
back: Go to plan B or still hunt (Tip).

front: Heart or lung hit reaction?
back: Often a kick or hard bolt, then a crash nearby (Tip).

front: Gut hit reaction?
back: Tail clamped, hunched, slow walk. Wait 6 to 8 hours or overnight if cool (70%).

front: Liver hit wait?
back: 4 to 6 hours (70%).

front: First thing at a downed white tail?
back: Notch (cancel) the species licence (99%, page 11 item 1).

front: Evidence of sex on a white tail doe?
back: Unskinned tail plus part of the udder and teats (99%, page 15).

front: Evidence of sex on a white tail buck?
back: Unskinned tail plus a testicle or part of the penis (99%, page 15).

front: Region 3 white tail bag?
back: 2, either sex. Aggregate deer bag 3, mule deer 1 (99%, page 33).

front: Distance rule near houses?
back: No hunting or shooting within 100 m of a dwelling or occupied farm or ranch building (99%, page 10).
